items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: my two big sisters that loved music and loved – had these wonderful record collections from Judy Collins to The Beatles to Eric Dolphy

ctx.x: Did it run in the family?

Not – well my two sisters, I had two big sisters that loved music and loved – had these wonderful record collections from Judy Collins to The Beatles to Eric Dolphy, or the Pentangle, I used to joke about The Pentangle. Very sixties. So I had two big sisters, five years older and two years older, and that set some sparks I think, but they did not become professional musicians, but one is a very fine poet in Western Mass, she’s in the Greenfield, Massachusetts area. But from, so not music boundary pushers from my…

classical musicians who could play with a great jazz feeling, like Gunther Schuller or like Jimmy Buffington. But people who are real improvisers, there weren’t that many at the time when I was say 17 or 18. But it was slowly growing and it dawned on me that – and I was just a very stubborn kid. It was like this is what I want to do, and so I just kept at it.
